proof_summary: Binomial absorption and coefficient extraction rewrite the relevant difference as \(\beta(pS,pN)-\beta(S,N)\), where \(\beta(S,N)=[x^N]\,G(x)(1-x)^{-S}\) and \(G(x)=(1-2x)/((1-x)(1-x+x^2))\). Expanding with \(\Delta=x^p+(1-x)^p=1+ph\), a Cartier fixed-point identity for \(G\), the factorization \(h=(1-x)(1-x+x^2)\eta\), and an antisymmetry cancellation remove the low-order terms; Kummer–Legendre/Stirling valuation bounds together with a product identity for the remaining Stirling-binomial sums then give every error term valuation at least \(3(v+1)\), applied with \(v=k-1\).
